findings: server shutdown_complete only after natural wait or both stop(5) and waiter finish. Stop failure/second cancellation/waiter exception do not release prematurely.
Independent release exception propagates to prevent normal exit. Cleanup does not replace a preexisting exception if reached while one is active.

Pool Release rejects outstanding borrowers before any unregister. Failed unregister retains ownership and does not free; successes are immediately removed from both sets and cannot be freed again. released_ only after complete success.
Destructors catch exceptions. Retrying remaining failed registrations during destructor does not retry prior successes; permanently failed memory may remain until process exit.

ReleaseMemoryPool orders DrainAsyncTasks then ClearMem then pool release. Each future.get observes task completion/result/exception before pop and keeps draining after error. It logs historical task failures rather than rethrowing them; no-new-producers after grpc shutdown is an explicit precondition.
Final log says release attempts finished with failure count before an exception; it no longer ambiguously claims completed release.
